newsitem.title: CHINA: China police clear Tiananmen Square of public.
newsitem.headline: China police clear Tiananmen Square of public.

text.p: Chinese police began clearing Tiananmen Square ahead of the memorial rites on Tuesday for deceased paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
A wall of police walked down the square, politely ushering people off the huge plaza beside the Great Hall of the People where 10,000 people will gather for the final farewell to Deng.
Police formed a cordon, positioned at intervals of about 3 metres (10 ft), all around the edge of the vast square.

Police as well as armed paramilitary People's Armed Police, with white flowers of mourning pinned to their uniforms, had swept slowly from north to south down the square that is a potent symbol of China and a focus for expressions of grief as well as demonstrations of anger.

Police gently ushered away an old couple from the eastern port city of Yantai who tried to lay a wreath of paper flowers to Deng at the square's central Monument to the Revolutinary Martyrs. "Old man Xiaoping, old man Xiaoping," the old woman wept as police gently led her away.

Chinese authorities have thrown a tight security net around the city, eager to prevent a repeat of the student-led demostrations that convulsed Beijing in 1989 after the death of another Communist Party luminary.
